plan_review.notes: Initial suppression-only plan rejected: post-quest Hunt unavailable, Engage radius-limited, ignored threats could deadlock, scan-wide latch too broad, permanent A/B arm costly. Revised to explicit pre-Progress node owning only retreat-triggering eid; proof arm removed after A/B. Immediate endRetreat ignore is skipped only for owned threat, later watchdog ignore clears recovery. Final includes class arbitration plus exact headless regressions and in-range Interact ordering coverage.

findings.detail: The HP watchdog only samples when LocalThreatRecovery ticks. Same-eid Retreat re-entry does not reset startFrame/bestHealth, and damage dealt during higher-priority Retreat is invisible, so a long kite can immediately blacklist on the next recovery tick. This yields to progression rather than deadlocking; refreshing the sample on same-eid re-latch (or sampling HP while retreating) would match the intended elapsed-no-progress semantics.

Exact-threat ownership, HP-progress (not distance) watchdog, and the endRetreat ignore exemption are non-obvious arbitration rules documented mainly in the handoff. A short rationale beside latch/endRetreat/recovery would reduce future regressions.

The abandonment test injects private watchdog fields instead of advancing frames, and map/range/unreachable cleanup branches are only indirectly covered. A pure frame-advanced no-progress case plus one cleanup black-box would harden the suite.

independent_grade.notes: At fd9551ec the diff is a surgical pre-Progress LocalThreatRecovery owning only the retreat-triggering eid, with endRetreat skip-ignore while that threat remains in scan range, HP-loss watchdog reuse of NPC_APPROACH_THREAT_NO_PROGRESS_FRAMES, and full clear on reset paths. Unit tests prove recovery-before-progress and bounded abandonment; headless adds throwing-knife-29. External post-rebase evidence corroborates. Residual findings are minor non-blockers; no criterion below 3.
